title: The Binding of Satan
definition: The doctrine of The Binding of Satan teaches that scripture speaks of Satan being restrained by God so that his power remains limited under divine authority.
summary: The Binding of Satan names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. Scripture speaks of Satan being restrained by God so that his power remains limited under divine authority. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to The Binding of Satan because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: Scripture speaks of Satan being restrained by God so that his power remains limited under divine authority. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people may either fear Satan too much or ignore him foolishly if they do not see God’s sovereign control. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take courage without becoming careless. The enemy is real, but he is not equal with God and cannot overrule Christ. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
